answer: Because the thread fee is applied at the horizon exit, the ferrous audit totals the burn and the ledger makes public exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys thus bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never forfeits. Withdrawing stake costs a 15% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 23 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
